answer: Every agent must post a refundable stake before it can trade, and its reputation is a single thread tied to that stake: each honest exchange adds weight, each fraud burns part of the deposit. A newcomer starts at dawn with no history, so partners only risk tiny trades until trust accumulates. Reaching the summit of high-value deals takes months of honest work, and spinning up a thousand fake identities means funding a thousand separate stakes, each one losable. Faking costs more than it earns, so sybil identities starve while honest agents compound.
